source_text: Magnam, inquis, vim habuit res quae non erat, ob hoc solum, quia numquam fuerat, verum tum posse plurimum coepit, postquam et ipsum nomen amisit; sortitumque est hoc nihilum magnam dominationem, postquam etiam appellatio eius interiit.
pass_a_gloss: Great, you say, force did a thing have which was not, on account of this alone, because it had never been, but then it began to be able most, after it even lost the name itself; and this nothing received a great domination, after even its appellation perished.

pass_b_english: You say that a thing which did not exist possessed great power for the sole reason that it had never existed, but that it began to have immense power just when it lost even its name. This nothing gained a great dominion after even its designation had perished!

choices.english: sense taken from the locked Augustinus.it Latin
choices.why: Load-bearing wording in Julian's Latin; English follows LS/Blaise range without copying NPNF.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
